column2: Space them out on the tray; brush with egg yolk and dip in sesame seeds.
Bake for 18–20 minutes until lightly golden on top and underneath.
Don’t add all the flour at once; the dough should stay soft.
You can use nigella seeds instead of sesame.
Serve with tea.
Keeps 1 week in a closed tin.
Date and walnut energy balls
1 cup pitted dates
3 tablespoons desiccated coconut
If the dates are hard, soak them in lukewarm water for 10 minutes and drain.
Pulse the walnuts and oats in a food processor until they look like coarse sand.
Add the dates and cocoa and process until it comes together like a dough.
With wet hands, roll hazelnut-sized pieces into balls.
Roll them in desiccated coconut.
Chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.
No cooking needed; you can make them with children.
For walnut allergies, use more oats instead; whole nuts are not given to young children, which is why they are finely ground here.
Serve 1–2 as a snack.
Keeps 1 week in a closed container in the fridge.
Red lentil and bulgur patties
1 cup fine bulgur for köfte
Wash the lentils and cook them in the water, stirring now and then, for about 15–20 minutes until they break down.
Take off the heat, stir in the bulgur and leave covered for 20 minutes to swell.
Meanwhile, chop the onion finely and soften it in the olive oil for 5 minutes; add both pastes and fry for 1 minute.
Add the fried onion, herbs, cumin, salt and lemon juice to the lentil mixture.
Knead with wet hands for 3–4 minutes; the mixture should be lukewarm.
Shape by squeezing in your palm and arrange on a serving plate.
If the mixture is dry, add a few spoonfuls of warm water.
All ingredients are cooked, so there is no raw egg or raw meat.
Serve with lettuce leaves and lemon wedges.
Borlotti bean and vegetable casserole
Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Dice the aubergine and leave in salted water for 10 minutes; squeeze and drain.
Chop the courgette, carrot, onion, pepper and tomatoes to a similar size.
Toss all the vegetables and the beans with olive oil and salt in a large bowl.
Put the mixture in a casserole dish, add the hot water and cover with foil.
Bake for 30 minutes; remove the foil and bake 15 minutes more until the vegetables are soft and lightly browned on top.
If using dried borlotti beans, soak them overnight and boil for 40–50 minutes.
Let the casserole rest for 10 minutes after taking it out of the oven.
Serve warm; yoghurt goes well alongside.
Chickpeas with garlic yoghurt (fatteh style)
2 slices of stale pide or lavash
2 tablespoons parsley
Cut the bread into small squares and toast them in a 200°C oven or a dry pan for 8–10 minutes until crisp.
Heat the chickpeas in their cooking liquid and season with cumin and salt.
Spread the bread over the base of the serving dish and top with the drained hot chickpeas.
Spread the garlic yoghurt over the chickpeas.
Melt the butter, add the chilli flakes and, once foaming, drizzle over the yoghurt and sprinkle with parsley.
Serve before the bread softens.
Use less garlic to make it suitable for children.
Store the components separately; don’t keep it once assembled.
Green lentil and spinach soup
7 cups hot water
Wash the lentils; wash the spinach and chop roughly.
Chop the onion, carrot and garlic small.
Heat the olive oil in a pan, sauté the onion and carrot for 5 minutes and add the garlic.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 1 minute.
Add the lentils and hot water; cook with the lid ajar over low heat for 30–35 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Add the spinach, cumin and salt and boil for 5 more minutes.
Serve with a squeeze of lemon juice.
If the soup thickens, add hot water.
For a more filling soup, add 2 tablespoons of rice.
Serve hot; you can drizzle chilli oil on top.
